title: Act on Compensation, Etc. for Persons Related to the May 18 Democratization Movement
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to promote the stability of the livelihoods and the welfare of persons related to the May 18 Democratization Movement and their surviving family members, and further to contribute to national reconciliation and democratic development, by having the State restore their honor and provide substantive compensation accordingly. <Amended on June 8, 2021>

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Act are defined as follows:
1. The term "May 18 Democratization Movement" means the democratization movement carried out by citizens in resistance to crimes that destroyed the constitutional order and crimes against humanity that occurred around December 12, 1979 and May 18, 1980;
2. The term "related person" means a person determined, following deliberation by the Committee for Deliberating Compensation for Persons Related to the May 18 Democratization Movement under Article 4, to fall under any of the following:
(a) A person who died or went missing in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement;
(b) A person who sustained an injury in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement;
(c) A person recognized as having suffered from a disease prescribed by Presidential Decree, or having died from the aftereffects thereof, in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement;
(d) A person who suffered sexual violence in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement;
(e) A person who was wanted, taken into custody, or detained in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement;
(f) A person whose prosecution was dismissed, who received a judgment of conviction or a judgment discharging the defendant from prosecution, or who was dismissed from employment or subjected to academic disciplinary action in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement.

Article 2-2 (Scope of Surviving Family Members)
(1) The term "surviving family members" in this Act means the heirs to a related person's property under the Civil Act: Provided, That, in the case of a missing person, those who would have become heirs to that person's property under the Civil Act at the time the person went missing shall be deemed surviving family members. <Amended on June 8, 2021>
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a spouse among a related person's surviving family members shall include a person in a de facto marital relationship with the related person: Provided, That a spouse or a person in a de facto marital relationship shall be excluded if, after marrying or entering into a de facto marital relationship with the related person, the spouse or person is or has been in a de facto marital relationship with another person. <Newly inserted on June 8, 2021>
(3) Surviving family members under paragraph (1) shall share the right to receive compensation and livelihood support benefits prescribed in this Act in accordance with their respective shares of inheritance under the Civil Act: Provided, That a person in a de facto marital relationship with a related person under paragraph (2) shall share the right to receive compensation and livelihood support benefits in accordance with the spouse's share of inheritance under the Civil Act. <Amended on June 8, 2021>

Article 3 (Committee for Supporting Compensation for Persons Related to the May 18 Democratization Movement)
(1) A Committee for Supporting Compensation for Persons Related to the May 18 Democratization Movement (hereinafter referred to as the "Compensation Support Committee") shall be established under the Prime Minister to support compensation and other measures for related persons and their surviving family members under this Act.
(2) The Compensation Support Committee shall perform the following functions:
1. Supporting compensation and other measures for related persons and their surviving family members;
2. Taking measures necessary to restore the honor of related persons;
3. Raising and managing donations to support related persons or their surviving family members;
4. Preparing measures to secure financial resources for compensation and other measures for related persons or their surviving family members;
5. Supporting projects related to the May 18 Democratization Movement;
6. Providing other support for related persons and their surviving family members.
(3) The Compensation Support Committee shall consist of not more than 15 members, including one chairperson. The Prime Minister shall serve as chairperson, and the Prime Minister shall appoint or commission the members from among persons with extensive knowledge and experience and relevant public officials, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(4) Matters necessary for the organization, operation, and other aspects of the Compensation Support Committee shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 4 (Committee for Deliberating Compensation for Persons Related to the May 18 Democratization Movement)
(1) A Committee for Deliberating Compensation for Persons Related to the May 18 Democratization Movement (hereinafter referred to as the "Compensation Deliberation Committee") shall be established in Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City to examine facts concerning related persons and their surviving family members and to deliberate and decide on compensation and other matters under this Act. <Amended on March 5, 2026>
(2) The Compensation Deliberation Committee shall perform the following functions:
1. Examining and deciding whether a person qualifies as a related person or a surviving family member thereof;
2. Determining the disability grades of related persons who sustained injuries;
3. Deliberating and deciding on, and paying, compensation and other benefits for related persons or their surviving family members;
4. Preparing proposals to be submitted to meetings of the Compensation Support Committee and handling matters delegated by the Compensation Support Committee;
5. Providing other support for related persons and their surviving family members.
(3) The Compensation Deliberation Committee shall consist of not more than 15 members, including one chairperson. The Mayor of Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City shall serve as chairperson, and the Prime Minister shall appoint or commission the members from among persons with extensive knowledge and experience and relevant public officials, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on March 5, 2026>
(4) The Compensation Deliberation Committee may establish subcommittees, each consisting of not more than 10 members, respectively for the examination under paragraph (2) 1 and the determination under paragraph (2) 2.
(5) Matters necessary for the organization, operation, and other aspects of the Compensation Deliberation Committee and its subcommittees shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 4-2 (Recommendation for Reinstatement)
The Compensation Support Committee may recommend to the State, a local government, or an employer that a related person who has been dismissed from employment be reinstated, if the related person so wishes.

Article 4-3 (Recommendation for Expungement of Academic Disciplinary Records)
The Compensation Support Committee may recommend to the school at which a related person was enrolled that it expunge the person's academic disciplinary records related to the May 18 Democratization Movement, reinstate the person as a student, and award the person an honorary diploma.

Article 5 (Compensation)
(1) Related persons or their surviving family members shall be paid compensation consisting of the amount calculated according to the following categories, plus interest at the statutory interest rate up to the time of the compensation decision: <Amended on December 30, 2025>
1. Surviving family members of a person who died or was confirmed to have gone missing in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement: The amount obtained by multiplying the person's monthly salary, actual monthly income, or average wages at the time of death or disappearance by the period of future employability calculated as of that time, less interim interest deducted using the simple discount method at the statutory interest rate;
2. A person who sustained an injury in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement, or the person's surviving family members: The sum of the following amounts:
(a) If necessary medical treatment results in a loss of income from monthly salary, actual monthly income, or average wages, the amount of that loss during the period of medical treatment;
(b) If the injured person has a physical disability, the amount obtained, according to the degree of loss of working capacity caused by the disability, by multiplying the person's monthly salary, actual monthly income, or average wages at the time of injury by the rate of loss of working capacity and the period of future employability calculated as of that time, less interim interest deducted using the simple discount method at the statutory interest rate;
3. A person who suffered sexual violence in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement: The amount prescribed by Presidential Decree in consideration of the severity of the harm and other relevant factors.
(2) If a person who sustained an injury in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement dies from a cause other than that injury, compensation under paragraph (1) 2 shall be paid as if the person were alive.
(3) The monthly salary, actual monthly income, or average wages under paragraph (1) shall be established by a certificate issued by the head of the Si, Gun, or Gu or the head of the tax office having jurisdiction over the person's domicile, or by other credible certification; where such income cannot be established, Presidential Decree shall govern.
(4) When calculating compensation under paragraph (1), living expenses prescribed by Presidential Decree shall be deducted from the monthly salary, actual monthly income, or average wages.
(5) The period of employability, disability grades, and rates of loss of working capacity under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 6 (Medical Support Benefits)
(1) A person who sustained an injury in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement and who, at the time this Act enters into force, requires continuing treatment, constant nursing care, or the use of assistive devices because of that injury shall be paid, in a lump sum, the actual costs of treatment, nursing care, and the purchase of assistive devices, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on June 8, 2021>
(2) When medical support benefits under paragraph (1) are paid, interim interest shall be deducted using the simple discount method at the statutory interest rate.

Article 6-2 (Special Cases concerning Persons Eligible for Medical Benefits)
Related persons and their surviving family members under this Act shall be deemed persons recognized by the Minister of Health and Welfare as requiring medical benefits pursuant to Article 3 (1) 8 of the Medical Care Assistance Act.

Article 6-3 (Support for Medical Benefits)
Medical benefits may be provided to persons who have received other support benefits under Article 22 and whom the Minister of Health and Welfare recognizes as requiring medical benefits.

Article 7 (Livelihood Support Benefits)
(1) The Compensation Deliberation Committee may pay support benefits to related persons or their surviving family members to assist with their livelihoods.
(2) Livelihood support benefits under paragraph (1) may be paid from donations made to support related persons, and the Government may provide part of the financial resources therefor.

Article 8 (Applications for Payment of Compensation and Other Benefits)
(1) A related person or a surviving family member thereof who wishes to receive compensation, medical support benefits, or livelihood support benefits under this Act (hereinafter referred to as "compensation and other benefits") shall apply in writing to the Compensation Deliberation Committee for payment of compensation and other benefits, attaching the relevant supporting documents as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Applications for payment of compensation and other benefits under paragraph (1) shall be made between July 1, 2023 and December 31, 2023. <Amended on December 27, 2022>

Article 9 (Deliberation and Decision)
The Compensation Deliberation Committee shall decide whether to pay compensation and other benefits and the amount thereof within 90 days from the date it receives an application for payment of compensation and other benefits. However, in the case of a missing person, the decision shall be made within 120 days.

Article 10 (Service of Written Decisions)
(1) Where the Compensation Deliberation Committee decides to pay or not to pay compensation and other benefits, it shall serve an authenticated copy of the written decision on the applicant within 30 days.
(2) The provisions of the Civil Procedure Act concerning service shall apply mutatis mutandis to service under paragraph (1).

Article 11 (Reconsideration)
(1) A related person or a surviving family member thereof who objects to a matter decided by the Compensation Deliberation Committee under Article 9 may apply to the Compensation Deliberation Committee for reconsideration within 30 days from the date the written decision is served under Article 10.
(2) Articles 9 and 10 shall apply mutatis mutandis to reconsideration by the Compensation Deliberation Committee and service, respectively. In such cases, "90 days" and "120 days" in Article 9 shall each be construed as "60 days."

Article 11-2 (Physical Examinations for Reclassification)
(1) The Compensation Deliberation Committee shall conduct a physical examination for reclassification of a person who has become subject to this Act after being assigned an injury grade of Other Grade 1 or Other Grade 2, where the Committee deems, upon that person's application, that reclassification of the injury grade is necessary. <Amended on December 27, 2022>
(2) A person who wishes to undergo a physical examination for reclassification under paragraph (1) shall apply for reclassification of the injury grade between July 1, 2023 and December 31, 2023. <Newly inserted on December 27, 2022>
(3) Matters necessary for the procedures for physical examinations for reclassification under paragraph (1) and other relevant matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on December 27, 2022>

Article 12 (Applicant's Consent and Payment of Compensation and Other Benefits)
(1) An applicant who has been served with an authenticated copy of a written compensation decision shall, in order to receive compensation and other benefits, request payment of compensation and other benefits from the Compensation Deliberation Committee without delay, attaching a written statement of consent to the decision.
(2) Matters necessary for the procedures for payment of compensation and other benefits and other relevant matters, other than those provided for in paragraph (1), shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 13 (Protection of the Right to Receive Compensation and Other Benefits)
The right to receive compensation and other benefits under this Act may not be transferred, provided as security, or attached.

Article 14 (Tax Exemption)
No national or local taxes shall be imposed on compensation and other benefits under this Act.

Article 15 (Requirement of a Prior Decision)
(1) An action concerning payment of compensation and other benefits under this Act may be brought only after the Compensation Deliberation Committee has made a decision to pay compensation and other benefits or to reject the application. However, this shall not apply where 90 days have elapsed from the date an application for payment of compensation and other benefits was made.
(2) An action under paragraph (1) shall be brought within 60 days from the date an authenticated copy of the written decision (including an authenticated copy of a written decision on reconsideration) is served.

Article 16 (Relationship with Compensation, etc. under Other Acts)
(1) This Act shall not apply to a person eligible for honorable treatment or support under the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons, Etc. of Distinguished Service to the State or the Act on Support for Persons Eligible for Veterans Compensation in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement.
(2) Where a person has received compensation or damages from the State or a local government under the Act on Restoration of Honor of and Compensation to Persons Related to Democratization Movements or the State Compensation Act in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement, compensation and other benefits under this Act shall be paid after deductions, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Newly inserted on June 8, 2021>
(3) Where the applicant consents to a decision to pay compensation and other benefits under this Act, a judicial settlement under the Civil Procedure Act shall be deemed to have been reached with respect to the harm suffered in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement. However, this shall not apply to psychological harm among the harm suffered in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement. <Amended on June 8, 2021; December 27, 2022>

Article 17 (Recovery of Compensation and Other Benefits)
(1) Where a person who has received compensation and other benefits under this Act falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the State may recover all or part of the compensation and other benefits received by that person:
1. Where the person has received compensation and other benefits by fraud or other improper means;
2. Where payment was made in error;
3. Where a person confirmed to have gone missing in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement is found to be alive or to have died or gone missing for reasons unrelated to the May 18 Democratization Movement.
(2) Where the State recovers compensation and other benefits under paragraph (1), it shall follow the procedures for the collection of national taxes.

Article 18 (Investigation of Facts and Duty to Cooperate)
(1) For the purposes of compensation and other measures under this Act, the Compensation Deliberation Committee may hear testimony or statements from related persons, witnesses, or persons with relevant knowledge or, where it deems necessary, conduct inspections or necessary investigations and other inquiries, and may request necessary cooperation from administrative agencies or other relevant institutions.
(2) A relevant institution requested to cooperate under paragraph (1) shall give priority to the request over other duties and notify the Compensation Deliberation Committee of the results without delay.

Article 19 (Extinctive Prescription)
The right to receive compensation and other benefits under this Act shall be extinguished by prescription if it is not exercised for one year from the date an authenticated copy of the written decision on payment of the compensation and other benefits is served on the applicant.

Article 19-2 (Counseling and Treatment Programs for Victims of Sexual Violence)
(1) The State shall operate counseling and treatment programs for the physical and psychological recovery of related persons falling under item (d) of subparagraph 2 of Article 2.
(2) The State may entrust the operation of counseling and treatment programs under paragraph (1) to medical institutions dedicated to sexual violence cases designated under Article 27(1) of the Act on the Prevention of Sexual Violence and Protection, etc. of Victims.
(3) Other matters necessary for the operation of counseling and treatment programs, the entrustment of their operation, and other relevant matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 20 (Solicitation of Donations)
(1) The Compensation Support Committee may solicit donations to provide support benefits to related persons and their surviving family members, etc. and to support the costs of projects related to the May 18 Democratization Movement.
(2) Solicitation of donations under paragraph (1) shall be deemed to have been registered under Article 4 of the Act on the Collection and Use of Donations.

Article 21 (Financial Support)
Where projects related to the May 18 Democratization Movement are undertaken, the Government may provide support for part of their costs.

Article 21-2 (Support for Foundations Related to the May 18 Democratization Movement)
(1) The State and local governments may, within budgetary limits, make contributions or provide support for expenses necessary for the projects and operation of foundations established for the purpose of carrying out commemorative projects related to the May 18 Democratization Movement.
(2) Matters necessary for the standards and procedures for contributions and support under paragraph (1) and other relevant matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 22 (Other Support Benefits)
(1) Support benefits may be paid, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, to persons deemed to require livelihood support in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement.
(2) Articles 7(2), 14, and 17 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the financial resources for and payment of support benefits under paragraph (1).

Article 23 (Special Provisions on the Period for Claiming Criminal Compensation)
(1) A related person or a surviving family member thereof who falls under any of the following subparagraphs may claim compensation within one year from the date this Act enters into force (meaning the date of entry into force of Act No. 18203, the Act Partially Amending the Act on Compensation, Etc. for Persons Related to the May 18 Democratization Movement), even if the claim period under Article 8 of the Act on Criminal Compensation and Restoration of Honor has elapsed:
1. A person who may claim compensation under Article 2 of the Act on Criminal Compensation and Restoration of Honor;
2. An heir who may claim compensation under Article 3 of the Act on Criminal Compensation and Restoration of Honor;
3. A person who may claim compensation under Article 26 of the Act on Criminal Compensation and Restoration of Honor;
4. A person who may claim compensation under subparagraphs 1 and 2 of Article 29(2) of the Act on Criminal Compensation and Restoration of Honor.
(2) A related person or a surviving family member thereof who falls under any of the following subparagraphs may claim compensation within one year from the date this Act enters into force (meaning the date of entry into force of Act No. 18203, the Act Partially Amending the Act on Compensation, Etc. for Persons Related to the May 18 Democratization Movement), even if the claim period under Article 28(3) of the Act on Criminal Compensation and Restoration of Honor has elapsed:
1. A person who may claim compensation under Article 27 of the Act on Criminal Compensation and Restoration of Honor;
2. A person who may claim compensation under subparagraph 3 of Article 29(2) of the Act on Criminal Compensation and Restoration of Honor.

ADDENDA <Act No. 4266, August 6, 1990>

Article 1 (Effective Date)
This Act shall enter into force 10 days after the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Transitional Measures)
(1) Where, before this Act enters into force, a person has been confirmed or reported, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, to have suffered harm in connection with the Gwangju Democratization Movement, that person shall be deemed to have applied for payment of compensation and other benefits under Article 8 on the date this Act enters into force.

(2) The examinations conducted by Gwangju Direct-Controlled City to determine whether persons reported pursuant to paragraph (1) qualify as persons related to the Gwangju Democratization Movement, and the investigations, medical examinations, etc. conducted by that City to determine the disability grades of injured related persons, shall be deemed to have been examinations, investigations, or medical examinations conducted by a subcommittee under Article 4 (4) of this Act.

(3) (Relationship with Other Statutes and Regulations) Where, at the time this Act enters into force, another statute or regulation cites the previous Act on Compensation, Etc. for Persons Related to the Gwangju Democratization Movement or any provision thereof, and this Act contains a corresponding provision, that citation shall be deemed to be a citation of this Act or the corresponding provision of this Act in lieu of the previous provision.
